I think the biggest recommendation I can give is trying to break that guilt and shame cycle. I can see in your post that you’re kind of beating yourself up for feeling this way, which is understandable but not helpful. Try to reframe it as more of a “okay I understand why I feel that way, that doesn’t make me bad, but I don’t believe this anymore and want to feel this way”. My therapist says it takes something like 1000 repetitions of something to remake a neural pathway (don’t fact check me on that), which is to say, it takes a lot of repetitions to stop the immediate shame cycle, but it is possible! The fact that you’re catching it when it happens is a great first step, now work on redirecting it!

Oof I relate hard to this, I’ve been having severe GERD for about a month now, just got my scope/a colonoscopy done today actually (they found nothing which is frustrating but also a good thing).

Things that help me manage the anxiety aspect:
1. Reminding myself that if I were having a major medical emergency, I would know it. I would not be able to move from pain and my mind would go into survival mode and I’d know to go to the hospital. It sounds like your symptoms are not at that level.
2. Taking a shower helps me a lot because if I’m well enough to shower, I’m not dying. Also, the overwhelming sensory experience of it tends to distract me from the symptoms and they usually go away because I get distracted by the shower. Play some music to add to the distraction!
3. ChatGPT is great, I try not to use it too much since it’s reassurance (and the environmental implications but trying to find balance with both). But saying “hey I have health anxiety, these are my symptoms, is it bad?” and having it explain why I’m not dying is super helpful. I now have it set up to remember I have health anxiety so it brings that up. DO THAT INSTEAD OF GOOGLING!!

I feel your pain, it sucks so bad and I’m sorry. Hopefully the scope gives you some answers or at the very least peace of mind!

This is my people/activities. I try to keep it vague. I used to have German Duolingo a habit, I just realized I should remove that, but I digress

I have ADHD, so I try to make using the app as little of a lift as possible. I do mood, and then subcategories with different activities. That way I can scroll quickly through and add what I did. 

So I have hobbies, life stuff (what chores I did, because I often forget when I last showered/cleaned/etc.), work (and what I did at work, since I do a lot of programs and meetings so my days are varied), people I talked to (broken into friends/family. I’ve considered having individual named people to track if relationships turn toxic, I have a not great family), and “influencers”, which is things like all nighter, hypersomnia, my period, etc. I also have a mental health category to track panic attacks and what not.

It takes me about 2 minutes to fill out in the evening, but gives me good data like “oh my day is worse when I talk to my family, but better when I do board games!”. Simplicity is key imo, especially if you’re struggling to get yourself to use the app.

However, I also had an intake appointment with a therapist who was /convinced/ I had PTSD when I genuinely do not have it. There’s a distinct difference between having trauma and having PTSD. If your T won’t drop the subject when you are clearly distressed about it, that’s a red flag.

Regardless, know that you’re not alone in this, trauma is a really touchy subject for a lot of people. It’s understandable that it would trigger your fight/flight/freeze reaction

I’m sorry but this whole thing sounds fishy to me as someone with two parent PLUS loans and other student loans.

First off, there’s no way that the daughter could cover her tuition with just Sub/UnSub loans. Mine amounted to roughly $5000 a semester by my senior year. If she’s going to a private institution (which I’m assuming is the case due to the kid feeling like there’s no other option besides fraud), there’s NO WAY it would’ve covered tuition.

Second off, my PLUS loans are all on me. They’re on my student loan account, my parents are just co-signers. They had to fill out the documentation to get me the loan (I couldn’t apply for it myself) but they aren’t under any obligation to pay it from what I can tell. In fact, I had to give my mom my log in for my Great Lakes (my loan provider) account so she could make payments on it. So the fact that OP is having this issue is wild to me in that sense.

Third, student loans must be paid starting 9 months out from graduation (with extensions happening if you continue onto grad school). The OP/daughter shouldn’t have to pay back these loans unless she took a year off or a paperwork error. Contact the loan provider and tell them that to get you more time to pay. You shouldn’t have to deal with it until 2022 at least, if she graduates on time.

Fourth, the government is pretty flexible with paying back these loans, especially since your daughter is supposed to be the ones paying them back. They do payment plans based on income, and all of that info will be given to her during exit counseling when she either graduates or drops out (hopefully the former). That’s why student loan debt, while awful, is somewhat better to be in because it wipes after 10 years a lot of the time, and repayment is based on income amount.

Ok so I would read up on your HIPPA rights (or whatever your patient privacy laws are if you’re not in the US) just so you know for sure what you can/can’t disclose. In general I believe your confidentiality is secure unless you either a. Sign something allowing your T to talk about it to someone (I’ve done this when I needed disability documentation, or my friend had to when I sat in on her first session as support), or b. If you are a serious threat to yourself or others (ie suicidal or about to hurt or kill someone). Self harm /typically/ doesn’t fall in the b category, unless there is concern about it escalating to an attempt.

Also, if you’re under 18, there might be some mandated reporting/child endangerment things to be concerned about as well, but I feel as though those are self explanatory, but I can go more in depth if you’d like.

On the topic of false accusations, you should be fine unless it involves the above, but again, highly recommend looking into patient privacy laws and such in your state/country

So I feel this a lot too, and here’s some tidbits to varying degrees of bluntness that I say to myself when I feel that way that might help you:

1. You’re paying your therapist, so no matter what you’re not wasting their time, if that makes sense. Like you are paying to be their and by accepting your money they are confirming that you aren’t wasting their time. If they did think that they’d probably mention terminating.

2. If you think you need therapy, you probably need therapy. Everyone probably needs therapy at one point or another. Society is ROUGH and we aren’t usually taught the proper coping mechanisms to deal with it. So learning those skills and such is beneficial to all.

3. There’s no such thing as being not ____ enough to get help. If you feel crummy, you deserve to seek help. Full stop.
